newsitem.title: UK: IPE oil futures ease from highs in choppy trade.
newsitem.headline: IPE oil futures ease from highs in choppy trade.

text.p: IPE Brent crude oil futures eased back from earlier highs on Friday amid busy trade.
June Brent stood at $18.73 a barrel at 1155 GMT, four cents up on the day, after earlier reaching up as high as $18.73.
June gas oil was $1.75 higher at $170.75.

"There is nothing really new out there, somebody is selling it off a bit," one broker said. "Volumes are very good at the moment because we have been seeing very good movements, good interest on the front spread, and volume attracts volume."
He said the June/July spread had moved from around 12 cents contango on Wednesday to the current four cents' backwardation.
The Brent cash market traded again in backwardation on Friday, with June/July sold early at +3 cents, compared with previous deals at -3 cents.
Dealers said that the International Energy Agency's end April report did not have any direct impact on prices.
The IEA said OPEC output rose 220,000 barrels per day in March, largely thanks to Iraq, while demand for that oil remained stagnant.
Technical analysts said prices were currently around a key previous resistance level and said the markets need to settle above $18.75 today to encourage the bulls.
